sentence: This project studies how lung cancers that have lost a certain gene respond to treatment, and how targeting replication stress affects that response.
This project studies how kidney cancers that lack a tumor suppressor protein can be attacked, and how inflammatory signaling affects immune cells in the tumor.
This project studies core fucosylation patterns in Alzheimer's disease to find biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
This project studies a protein found in white fat tissue to find out how it affects immunotherapy against breast cancer, including in patients who are obese.
This project studies how stiffer arteries change the behavior of smooth muscle cells in blood vessels, using porcine aorta material and a mouse model.
This project builds a method to map a chemical change on RNA across cancer cell lines, tumors and normal tissues.
This project tries to find out why some early blood conditions turn into cancer in some people but not in others.
This project studies how small packages released by brain immune cells made from stem cells affect recovery after stroke, using brain organoid models.
This project studies how brainstem circuits control rhythmic movements of the mouth and face, to learn why swallowing and breathing can go wrong.
This project builds computer tools that read patient records to find hospital patients at high risk of carrying or developing a drug-resistant bacterial infection.
This project studies how natural selection has shaped the X chromosome and how it contributes to health and disease.
This project studies what leads mothers to buy ultra-processed foods for toddlers, using several kinds of methods.
This project studies how a regulatory system controls bacteria that survive antibiotic treatment and wake up again within biofilms.
This project builds statistical and deep learning methods to interpret rare changes in human genes and their role in disease.
This project provides mouse models made by genome editing and other methods, and stores mouse lines, for research on digestive and liver diseases.
This project studies how blocking a fatty acid pathway in immune-suppressing cells can help immune cells attack tumors.
This project builds a screening platform to find ways of turning non-muscle cells into muscle cells more efficiently.
This project tests a drug combination against ovarian cancer that resists treatment, and tries to find out which tumors respond to it.
This project studies how the different embryonic origins of cells shape the formation of the shoulder girdle in zebrafish.
